title: Support Worker ( Female Only )
description:
Ashberry recruitment are currently seeking for an experienced Female support worker in the housing sector, to work as part of a wonderful team at a Service in Sheffield which provide daily support and supported accommodation to female individuals suffering from homelessness, substance misuse and mental health issues.

This is a permanent post and the successful candidate will be required to work full time 40 hours per week. This post involves some weekend working.

ABOUT THE JOB & SERVICE

This Service is ran by a well established housing organisation and charity, who for years have provided housing support, advice and supported accommodation to vulnerable individuals across the UK.

As a support worker for this service, the successful candidate will be expected to:
- Facilitate client meetings and other client participation methods.
- Conduct regular client support plan reviews, completing and updating individual support plans.
- Work with clients to achieve their identified goals in accordance with company policy, including client benefits being maximised and personal payments are made as part of a budget plan.
- Work with colleagues to design and deliver a range of in-house support provisions designed to achieve successful outcomes.
- Delegate to and coordinate the work of Assistant Support workers with clients, to ensure actions as identified in client support plans, are addressed in a timely professional and appropriate manner.
- Complete and review client's assessments including risk assessments, within contractual timeframes, using a person-centred and trauma sensitive approach.
- Respect the diversity of other people's culture, faith and practice.
- Ensure all practice is in line with relevant legislation, guidelines and polices to protect clients, colleagues, staff and visitors from any abuse, accident or injury.
- Complete any other duties as could be reasonably expected in the fulfilment of this role.

An Enhanced Child and Adult DBS is required for this role.

DESIRED ATTRIBUTES

-NVQ level 3 or equivalent in related field

-Previous experience working in a supported housing or Hostel/Lifehouse setting

-Knowledge of Government policy governing homelessness

-Knowledge of local housing market and how to access accommodation for clients

-First Aid training

-Knowledge of the main support needs which are commonly faced by homeless and vulnerable clients

-Ability to work in a busy environment and can demonstrate ability to make decisions under pressure

-Knowledge of the benefits system and an understanding of supported housing funding streams

-Ability to use your initiative in problem solving for the benefit of clients and colleagues

-Excellent verbal and written communication skills

-The ability to understand and successfully implement processes, procedures and policies related to your area of work

-Previous experience of successfully working within a team environment to meet objectives

-Good IT skills with previous experience of using Microsoft Office, email programmes and databases

Please don't hesitate to apply or contact us today for further information

PLEASE NOTE: We advise candidates to apply as soon as they can as applications for this job may close at any time dependant on the amount of applicants are put forward.

title: Stroke Support Worker
description:
Stroke Support Worker

We are looking for an empathetic, adaptable individual, experienced in person centred support to work with stroke survivors and their loved ones on the stroke ward in Doncaster Royal Infirmary.

Position: 000029 Stroke Support Worker

Location: Homebased, Doncaster, South Yorkshire. However, travel will be required twice weekly to Doncaster Royal Infirmary as part of this role (and occasional wider travel may include team meetings or other work-related meetings)

Hours: 21 - 28 hours per week with a minimum of 21 hours. The exact weekly hours (up to 28) will be agreed with the successful candidate

Salary: £17,000 - £22,600 per annum depending on hours (FTE circa £28,340.58)

Contract: 12 month fixed term contract

Benefits: 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays (this will increase with service up to 30 days, full time equivalent) cashback and discount scheme, employee assistance programme, learning and development, pension scheme, Life Assurance, Eye Care vouchers, Long Service Award, Health Cash Plan, flexible working opportunities available.

Closing Date: Sunday 9 August 2026

Interview Date: Provisionally 19 August 2026

The Role

This work is part of a project (the Integrated Offer), exploring the needs and ongoing connection for people affected by stroke in hospital and beyond.

The role will involve delivering person-centred stroke support in the hospital setting, while working with the Integrated Offer team to test and implement new approaches. The areas we aim to deliver and test are:
- Deliver person centred conversations with people affected by stroke on the acute ward.
- Following an initial conversation, test how people affected by stroke connect with the Association next, and what they connect to.
- Explore how to increase connection with those who are not present on the ward at the same time as us.

(note- we may test some or all the above)

To support flexible delivery and testing, you'll also develop your skills by providing phone support to people affected by stroke.

The role includes working in Doncaster Royal Infirmary starting with twice weekly visits, for 3 hours per session. These sessions can be any time after 11am. The length, timing and cadence of the sessions may need to adjust as this is a test and we will be led by what works for the hospital and people affected by stroke.

Occasional overnight stays may be required.

About You

Key skills/experience:
- Experience of communicating directly with people affected by stroke, either on the phone or face to face.
- Experienced in person centred support Emotional intelligence and good judgement skills
- Effective listening skills with the ability to communicate clearly at a time where emotions may be heightened.
- High levels of emotional resilience to handle complex situations whilst working in a hospital environment.
- Ability to embrace the principles of coaching and reflective practice to drive continuous improvement.

To fulfil the role, you must be a resident of the UK and have the right to work in the UK.

Applications

You will be asked to submit your CV, (including details of your current address), and a supporting statement of no more than two pages, demonstrating how you meet the person specification and what you bring to the role in terms of your skills and experience. Please also state your availability, and the hours you would like to discuss.

If you are applying under the Disability Confident scheme, please indicate this in your supporting statement, and in the main body of your email when applying for the role.

You will be able to view the role profile when you apply.

Finding strength through support

The organisation is the only charity in the UK providing lifelong support for all stroke survivors and their families. Providing tailored support to tens of thousands of stroke survivors each year. This support includes one-to-one and group support, funding vital scientific research into stroke prevention, acute treatment, recovery and long-term care, and campaigning to secure the best care for everyone affected by stroke.

They are here for stroke survivors and their loved ones, from the moment they enter the new and frightening post-stroke world, supporting them every step of the way as they find their strength and their way back to life.

It's only thanks to the generosity of supporters and donors that they can provide vital support.

The Association is driven by an ambition to improve the lives of everyone affected by stroke. This means they're determined to create an equitable and inclusive workplace that benefits from the difference, and thrives on the diversity, of our people. Guided by an approach to solving inequity in stroke, the team are prioritising listening to, and learning from, lived experience across the charity.

The charity are working to improve the representation of this lived experience at all levels within the Association and are eager to recruit applicants from a variety of communities and backgrounds. We are keen to receive applications from people affected by stroke, people of colour, members of LGBT+ communities, and disabled people because these identities and experiences are underrepresented and would add enormous value to how the organisation work.

A Disability Confident employer, the organisation is making great progress focusing on flexible working, reasonable adjustments and access to work. The charity has a variety of staff network groups and are committed to continuously improving diversity and inclusion efforts. If you have questions, or access needs, we're happy to discuss any support and adjustments we can make throughout the recruitment process so that you're able to contribute your best in a way that meets your needs.

You may also have experience in areas such as Care Coordinator, Stroke Support, Stroke, Care, Care Worker, Support Worker, Carer, Support Group, Support and Advice, Social Care, Ca

title: Therapeutic Family Support Worker / Parenting Practitioner
description:
Therapeutic Family Support Worker

Location: Barnsley (S71)Pay: £18 per hourType: Agency (12-week structured intervention)

About the RoleWe are seeking experienced and confident Therapeutic Family Support Workers / Parenting Practitioners to support an edge-of-care placement supporting a family in their home in Barnsley.

This is a high-impact, relationship-based role, focused on preventing breakdown by delivering consistent, therapeutic intervention within the home.

You will work as part of a structured support plan, helping the parent to develop effective parenting strategies while supporting the child's emotional and behavioural needs.

What You'll Be Doing
- Providing direct, relationship-based support to both parent and child within the family home
- Modelling and promoting positive parenting approaches and routines
- Supporting emotional regulation, behaviour management and de-escalation
- Working to a clear intervention plan in partnership with social care professionals
- Creating a safe, consistent and structured environment
- Supporting daily activities, engagement, and routine-building
- Recording observations and contributing to progress updates

Shift Pattern
- Early & late shift patterns 08:00 - 16:00 and 15:30 - 23:00
- Flexibility required, with occasional late shifts extending to late evening / midnight
- Rotational shift pattern as part of a wider support team

What We're Looking For
- Experience working with children and families in challenging or complex situations
- Background in roles such as:
- Family Support Worker
- Parenting Practitioner
- Youth / Outreach Worker
- Residential or Early Help services
- Strong understanding of:
- Trauma-informed practice
- Behaviour support and de-escalation techniques
- Attachment and relational working
- Ability to build trust and maintain professional boundaries
- Confidence working independently within a home environment
- Full UK driving licence (essential)

Desirable (but not essential)
- Training in Team Teach, PRICE, MAPA or similar (Training Available)
- Experience in edge-of-care / family preservation work
- Relevant qualifications (e.g. Level 3/4 Children & Young People, Health & Social Care)

What We Offer
- Competitive hourly rate with weekly pay
- Structured support and guidance throughout the placement
- Opportunity to work on a meaningful, outcome-focused intervention
- Further work opportunities available, as part of our wider social care team

ApplyIf you are passionate about working with families to create lasting change and preventing children entering care, we'd love to hear from you.

Please submit your CV outlining your relevant experience.

Family Support Worker

title: Waking Night Rehabilitation Support Worker
description:
Waking Night Rehabilitation Support Worker

Location: Barnsley

Salary: £13.45 per hour

Job Types: Part-time, Permanent

We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Waking Night Support Worker to provide high-quality care to individuals as they recover and relearn skills after they have had an accident or injury. The work we do at Ariya Neuro Care makes a profound impact on peoples' lives.
- We have achieved the highest level of Platinum in the Investors in People Accreditation due to the development of our staff.
- We were also shortlisted for the Investors in People 'Platinum Employer of the year 2025.
- All of our CQC inspected services are rated outstanding in all areas, because we genuinely care about the people we support. If you have a passion to help others this could be a good fit for you.

The role:

We're looking for a proactive person to join our rehabilitation service on nights. Our service in Worsborough is a high-quality environment, with a focus on developing people. We provide a great induction with supportive shadowing and further development opportunities.

The role is for 30 hours per week from 10pm until 8am and the shifts are on a rota, including some weekends. Training will be during day-time hours.

The ideal candidate would be happy working both on their own and within a team, be proactive and have a good sense of humour. The team are really friendly, welcoming and supportive and there are fabulous training and development opportunities.

The waking night team support individuals to develop a good sleep/ wake cycle, and offer reassurance and support overnight. This role also involves all aspects of personal care, cleaning duties and some paperwork to prepare the service for the next day.

Join us in making a difference in the lives of those we support!

Benefits:
- Employee mentoring programme
- Free flu jabs
- Free parking
- Health & wellbeing programme
- On-site parking
- Store discount

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Ariya Neurocare, please do not hesitate to apply.
